scope.continuity: Named literary work and stated period only
scope.period: The functioning human transition after power technology becomes available
scope.exclusions: The Grand Galactics’ long absence and later return are not continuous government; active uploads have a separate identity/support question.

after.description:
Power technology and uploads appear through interventions involving the One Point Fives and Machine Stored, while the Grand Galactics are absent for a long interval. The selected point is Earth’s energy-enabled human transition, not continuous direct alien rule. The guarantee best guess allows a partial material floor, qualified by the difference between abundant power and equal access to food, housing and care.

 Human institutions and productive users receive positive control weight, with external technical dependence inside the broad interval. Providing technology does not automatically make an absent alien authority the ongoing owner of every household. The moderate nonworking scenario permits routine substitution while counting research, maintenance, administration, services, care and useful creation. Energy output, uploads and long time spans are not participation statistics. Only living biological humans define this rate; inactive records and active uploaded communities are not silently mixed in. The partial-transition interpretation remains explicit rather than claiming an enacted universal constitution.

guarantees.basis: Transferred power can support a floor, but energy alone does not settle household rights.

control.basis: Human institutions retain agency during the absent-superpower period.

nonworking.basis: Biological humans retain useful roles; energy, uploads and elapsed years are not participation.

before.reason: The lead's continuous alien-rule label obscures distinct periods, while the material effect of the later technology remains unverified.
before.analysis: The secondary ending describes client aliens acting independently while the Grand Galactics are absent, followed by new power technology, mind uploading and a much later transfer of guardianship. Those changes may produce a suitable society, but neither cheap power nor digital existence alone proves automated subsistence or a nonworking share. The scientific protagonist's initial wealth is also not population-wide provision.
before.follow_up: Read the actual exchange and late-epilogue passages. Separate contemporary humans, any uploaded community and the distant successor order; qualify a record only after its productive and allocative rules are established.

after.name: Eden (the Doubler automated-factory order)

scope.continuity: Named literary work and stated period only
scope.period: The functioning Doubler society encountered by the crew
scope.population: Living biological Doubler residents, an explicit alien-person proxy
scope.exclusions: The factory’s recycling output is not automatically useful household provision; visiting humans have a separate predicament.

after.description:
The explorers encounter an automatic factory cycling through production, destruction and recycling in an oppressive alien society. The machinery is real, but its output is not assumed to supply equal useful necessities. The guarantee best guess is very weak because automatic capacity coexists with concealed political domination and uncertain access. This zero variant preserves that distinction instead of treating any operating factory as a post-scarcity welfare system.

 Concentrated biological institutional authority is central, with machine-controller alternatives inside the broad interval because outsiders struggle to interpret the system. Unfamiliar machinery does not automatically establish AI sovereignty. The modest nonworking scenario counts production, administration, maintenance, services, care and useful creation among living Doublers. Circular output, waste and factory throughput are not labor percentages. The crew’s survival tasks do not become the resident denominator. The alien-person proxy and wide bounds retain the familiar opaque society without requiring complete access to its fictional legal and economic institutions.

guarantees.basis: Automatic capacity and political domination do not imply secure useful access.

control.basis: Biological institutional power is central, with outsider uncertainty broad.

nonworking.basis: Living Doublers retain useful roles; recycling throughput and human visitors are not a census.

before.reason: Automatic machinery and an oppressive alien polity are established separately; a wage-independent household economy is not.
before.analysis: The factory scene confirms automatic operation, while a secondary summary describes an output-recycling loop. Such a plant may be economically disconnected or dysfunctional rather than a source of universal provision. The novel's difficulty of interpreting alien institutions also makes an unqualified global control point misleading. Neither advanced technology nor political violence answers how the Doublers obtain necessities.
before.follow_up: Read the later Doubler conversation and its account of current productive and allocative institutions. Verify who receives useful output and who must work; retain the factory as a lead rather than inventing a welfare or zero-variant regime.
